jobs.title: Business Operations Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

OpenFX is on a mission to move money as freely as data, unrestricted by time zones, banking hours, or legacy systems. We are building the infrastructure that will power the next generation of cross-border payment systems for institutions. The team's execution has been exceptional, and we're scaling at a remarkable pace. Our stellar early team comes with experience in companies like J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, FalconX, Paypal, Affirm, Polygon, Kraken, Nium & others. We’re backed by Accel, Lightspeed, NfX and other top-tier investors.

Role Overview

Business Operations is OpenFX's execution and coordination layer for business-critical initiatives that need several functions to work together: launching new currencies and regions, bringing banking and liquidity partners live, operationalising newly acquired licences, and fixing the cross-team processes that slow us down. The team is deliberately hands-on and horizontal. It creates clarity in ambiguous, high-priority problems, fills execution gaps, and stays with the work until it is delivered, then hands ongoing ownership back to the function that should own it.

We are hiring a Business Operations Manager based in the United States to be the single accountable owner for OpenFX's US banking and licence-operationalisation program, and to bring senior generalist capacity to the wider Business Operations portfolio. Today our US work is spread across several people in other time zones. This role consolidates it under one owner who works US hours, sits close to our US partners and regulators, and can carry programs sponsored directly by our executive team through to launch.

This is a builder's role in a regulated, multi-entity, multi-country business. You will spend most of your time with banks, custodians, liquidity providers and compliance vendors on one side, and with Legal, Compliance, Finance, Trade Operations, Product and Engineering on the other. You will be judged on whether things go live, not on how much activity you generate.

Key Responsibilities:

The role covers five areas. The first two are where you will spend most of your time in the first year.

- US banking program and partner onboarding.  Own the US bank-partner portfolio end to end: the near-term launch of USD account capabilities on a partner's licence, and the longer-term path to launching on OpenFX's own licences with scalable partners. Run the full onboarding cycle with sponsor banks, BaaS providers, custodians and liquidity partners: program structure, commercials, compliance questionnaires and due diligence, master agreements, and the integration gates with Product and Engineering. Build primary-plus-backup redundancy so no single partner can stall a launch. Be the US-hours relationship owner for our US banking counterparties.

- Licence operationalisation and launch readiness.  Turn approved or pending US money-transmission licences into a live, controlled operating program. You will own the readiness plan and the program management: defining and getting sign-off on the flow of funds, closing ownership and vendor scope for transaction monitoring, gathering ledger and reconciliation requirements, and landing onboarding tooling and operating controls before launch. You drive clear DRI ownership at the workstream level and escalate risks and decisions early. Legal and Compliance own licence strategy, application content, regulatory interpretation and formal submissions; you make sure the business is ready to operate on what they secure.

- Partner management and performance.  Act as the named Business Operations owner for an assigned set of active partners under our partner-management framework: maintain the partner and contract tracker, produce quarterly partner scorecards and stewardship memos, keep rate cards and commercial terms current for Finance, and contribute to the partner playbook that captures what we learn across selling, onboarding, go-live and ongoing management.

- Cross-functional program delivery across the Americas and beyond.  Bring senior generalist capacity to the team's wider portfolio when priorities demand it: Canadian settlement accounts, Latin American entity and banking setup, new-market and corridor discovery, compliance and custody tooling selections, and process improvements that span several Operations teams. Take ambiguous problems, build the plan, coordinate the functions involved, and hand the work back once it is running.

- Operating cadence and decision support.  Keep your programs accurately reflected in the Business Operations project tracker and weekly sync: outcome, owner, milestone, status, risks and decisions needed. Produce the business cases, opportunity assessments and operational-readiness recommendations leadership needs to make decisions, with assumptions, economics, dependencies and risks made explicit.

How this role works with other teams

Business Operations builds the plan and keeps shared work moving. Functional leaders continue to own their strategy, specialist decisions, controls and results. Legal and Compliance own licensing and regulatory content. Partnerships owns commercial partner strategy. Finance owns the books. Trade Operations owns settlement and exception handling. Product and Engineering own the roadmap and the build. When a program is complete, ongoing work is handed to the team that owns it rather than staying with Business Operations indefinitely.

What success looks like in the first six months

- The US banking program has a committed launch plan with a single owner, closed partner structure, signed agreements and a live primary partner, with a backup in onboarding.

- The flow of funds for US licensed operations is defined and approved, and the transaction-monitoring, ledger, reconciliation and onboarding workstreams each have a named DRI, a plan and a date.

- Every partner you own has a current scorecard, an up-to-date contract and rate card on file, and a stewardship memo delivered on the agreed cadence.

- Your programs are accurately reflected in the team tracker every week, risks reach the right decision maker before they become surprises, and functional leaders say Business Operations makes their work move faster without taking ownership away from them.

What we are looking for

Must-haves

- 8+ years of operating experience in fintech, payments, banking or another regulated financial-services environment, with meaningful time spent in business operations, strategy and operations, partnerships operations or program leadership.

- Direct, hands-on experience taking a financial product live with US banks: sponsor-bank or BaaS programs, FBO (for-benefit-of) account structures, money-transmitter-based programs, or equivalent. You have personally run bank due diligence, negotiated commercials and program agreements, and managed the integration gates to launch.

- Working knowledge of the US money-transmission landscape from an operator's seat: state licensing, BSA/AML program expectations, flow-of-funds design and the controls banks expect to see. You do not need to be a lawyer or compliance officer, but you need to hold your own with them.

- A record of leading complicated programs across many functions with clear personal ownership and measurable results, including examples where you consolidated fragmented work under one owner.

- Strong commercial and analytical judgment: you can read a fee schedule, model a program's economics, and turn incomplete information into a decision.

- Clear, direct written communication and executive judgment. You document decisions, surface problems early and make ownership and tradeoffs explicit.

- Comfort with ambiguity and pace. You set a way of working and move important work forward without waiting for a playbook.

- Based in the United States with the ability to travel to partners and to our Miami office as needed.

What helps you stand out

- Cross-border payments, FX or stablecoin experience, including custody providers and liquidity partners.

- Experience launching a US banking program from zero, or operationalising a newly acquired or newly granted licence.

- Experience building partner-management or vendor-management frameworks: scorecards, performance reviews, contract and commercial hygiene.

- Exposure to Canada or Latin America banking and entity setup.

- Experience in a high-growth company operating multiple regulated entities across several countries.

What We Offer

- Competitive salary and benefits package.

- Equity in a rapidly growing company.

- Opportunity to work in a fast-paced startup at the forefront of fintech innovation.

- Opportunity to make a significant impact on global financial infrastructure

- Collaborative work culture with emphasis on personal and professional growth.

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

jobs.title: Compliance Program Manager - Dora
jobs.description:
About Us

OpenFX is on a mission to move money as freely as data, unrestricted by time zones, banking hours, or legacy systems. We are building the infrastructure that will power the next generation of cross-border payment systems for institutions. The team's execution has been exceptional, and we're scaling at a remarkable pace. Our stellar early team comes with experience in companies like J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, FalconX, Paypal, Affirm, Polygon, Kraken, Nium & others. We're backed by Accel, Lightspeed, NfX and other top-tier investors.

Role Overview

We are looking for a Security & Compliance Engineer to turn regulatory requirements into real, running controls — and then prove to auditors that they work. This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who thrives in fast-paced, heavily regulated environments and knows how to make compliance provable in production rather than on paper.

OpenFX is expanding across Europe in a heavily regulated financial environment. As we scale into EU markets, regulators, auditors, and enterprise partners expect provable, continuously operating security controls — not slide decks or one-off audits. Compliance requirements (DORA, GDPR, SOC 2, ISO 27001, and region-specific regulations) are increasing faster than our ability to operationalize them, and this role exists to close that gap.

You will own the security controls and evidence that regulators and auditors care about, end to end — from translating regulatory language into concrete mechanisms through to audit walkthroughs and remediation. You will partner closely with Legal, Compliance, Risk, and engineering to ensure compliance is built into the platform rather than bolted on after the fact.

This role is based in Amsterdam, Netherlands (EU/EEA).

Key Responsibilities:

- Own audit-ready security controls

- Design, implement, and maintain technical and operational controls for DORA, GDPR, SOC 2, ISO 27001, and future regional requirements.

- Ensure controls are not just documented, but actually enforced in AWS, Kubernetes, and application layers.

- Be the technical counterpart to Legal, Compliance & Risk

- Translate regulatory language into concrete security mechanisms.

- Partner with Legal and Compliance to monitor new regulations and assess technical impact.

- Decide what is "good enough" vs. over-engineered for compliance.

- Run audits instead of reacting to them

- Own audit preparation, evidence collection, walkthroughs, and remediation tracking.

- Build repeatable, automated evidence pipelines instead of last-minute scrambles.

- Be the person auditors trust when they ask, "Show me how this actually works."

- Embed compliance into the platform

- Work with engineering to design systems that are secure by default and defensible to regulators.

- Ensure logging, access controls, encryption, monitoring, and change management meet regulatory expectations.

- Automate compliance wherever possible

- Build tooling and scripts to continuously validate controls (access reviews, logging coverage, config drift).

- Reduce manual compliance work over time by pushing checks into code and infrastructure.

What we are looking for

Must-haves:

- 6+ years in security engineering, cloud security, or compliance-focused security roles.

- Hands-on, operational experience implementing DORA in a production/regulated environment (not advisory only) — e.g. ICT risk management, incident classification and reporting, third-party/ICT vendor oversight, and digital operational resilience testing. GDPR implementation experience is a strong bonus.

- Experience supporting SOC 2 and/or ISO 27001 audits (strong plus).

- Ability to translate regulatory requirements into technical controls.

- Strong working knowledge of AWS security fundamentals (IAM, logging, encryption, networking).

- Comfortable owning auditor interactions and explaining systems clearly.

- Experience building or automating security/compliance processes (Python, Bash, Go, etc.).

- Accountability for an audit outcome — if you've never owned one, this role is not a fit.

What helps you stand out:

- Experience securing Kubernetes environments.

- Familiarity with AppSec tooling (SAST/DAST, manual testing).

- Experience with AWS security services (GuardDuty, Config, Security Hub).

- Prior work in fintech, payments, or regulated infrastructure.

- Security or compliance certifications (CISSP, CISA, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer, AWS Security).

- Familiarity with EU financial regulators and national competent authorities (e.g. DNB/AFM in the Netherlands, EBA/ESMA).

What We Offer

- Competitive salary and benefits package.

- Equity in a rapidly growing company.

- Opportunity to work in a fast-paced startup at the forefront of fintech innovation.

- Opportunity to make a significant impact on global financial infrastructure

- Collaborative work culture with emphasis on personal and professional growth.

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

jobs.description:
About Us

OpenFX is on a mission to move money as freely as data, unrestricted by time zones, banking hours, or legacy systems. We are building the infrastructure that will power the next generation of cross-border payment systems for institutions. The team's execution has been exceptional, and we're scaling at a remarkable pace. Our stellar early team comes with experience in companies like J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, FalconX, Paypal, Affirm, Polygon, Kraken, Nium & others. We’re backed by Accel, Lightspeed, NfX and other top-tier investors.

Role Overview

We're hiring a People Operations Lead to own and build the people operations function with a strong anchor in our Bangalore hub. This is a hands-on leadership role. You will be responsible for designing and running the core people operations infrastructure — onboarding, offboarding, employment compliance, benefits administration, HRIS management, employee relations, and performance frameworks — with a particular focus on getting India operations to a best-in-class standard while supporting our global footprint.

You would report to the COO and work closely with the Head of People Operations & Talent (once hired) as well as every functional leader in the company. In the near term, you will be the most senior people ops person on the ground in Bangalore, and the team and leadership will rely on you to be the operational backbone of how we manage our people.

This role requires someone who has built and scaled people operations before. You should have 10+ years of experience, with meaningful depth in India employment law, HR compliance, and people operations at a company that was scaling quickly. If you've only operated in steady-state environments or in a single-country context, this will be a stretch.

Key Responsibilities:

- Own end-to-end people operations for the Bangalore hub and support global people ops processes across the US, EU, UK, and UAE.

- Design and implement structured onboarding and offboarding programs that work across geographies.

- Manage the HRIS (Rippling) rollout and ongoing administration for India, ensuring data integrity and compliance.

- Build and maintain employment compliance frameworks for India, including labor law, benefits, leave policies, and statutory requirements.

- Develop and operationalize performance management processes, including review cycles, feedback mechanisms, and calibration support.

- Partner with legal and finance on employment-related matters including contractor-to-employee conversions, entity setup, and benefits benchmarking.

- Serve as the go-to person for employee relations issues in the Bangalore hub, handling sensitive situations with discretion and good judgment.

- Build the foundational people analytics — headcount tracking, attrition analysis, engagement surveys — to inform leadership decisions.

What we are looking for

Must-haves:

- 10+ years of experience in people operations or HR, with significant time spent at high-growth technology companies.

- Deep expertise in India employment law, HR compliance, and statutory requirements.

- Experience managing or implementing an HRIS (Rippling experience is a plus).

- Track record of building people ops processes from early stage — you've been the person who designed the onboarding, wrote the policies, and built the frameworks, not just maintained them.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills. We are async-heavy and globally distributed. You need to be effective in writing.

- Ability to operate with high autonomy. We will give you a charter and access to every leader in the company. We will not give you a playbook.

What helps you stand out:

- Experience supporting people operations across multiple countries (US, EU, UK, UAE in addition to India).

- Prior experience at a fintech or financial services company navigating regulatory complexity.

- Experience with PEO/EOR arrangements and contractor compliance across jurisdictions.

- Familiarity with Rippling as an HRIS platform.

- Experience building people analytics and reporting frameworks from scratch.

What We Offer

- Competitive salary and benefits package.

- Equity in a rapidly growing company.

- Opportunity to work in a fast-paced startup at the forefront of fintech innovation.

- Opportunity to make a significant impact on global financial infrastructure

- Collaborative work culture with emphasis on personal and professional growth.

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.
